name: Limit Break Payment Processor V2 forwarded-calldata offset sender spoof
summary: Payment Processor copied a forwarded call's trade data from the caller-supplied ABI offset but sized it as if canonical, so through a permissionless trusted forwarder attacker bytes became the ERC-2771 sender. Attackers acted as any wallet that had approved it: accepting zero-price offers for victims' NFTs and making victims buy worthless listings with approved tokens.
notes: Immutable PaymentProcessor V2 runtime holds the fixed-offset copy in its delegate-call wrapper; forwarders are permissionless clones and collection settings add no causal configuration. ApeChain's V3 shares the modifier and was hit by the same actors, so it is one campaign.

loss.usd is the exact ERC-20 debits of victims in spoofed buy-listing txs (re-measured from receipts on every chain). Stolen NFTs (tens of thousands of items) have no market price here and are not valued, so this is a lower bound; SlowMist reports about 2.8M USD.

Bundles are classified by party != tx sender from event logs, not traced one by one; sampled txs all route through a TrustedForwarder. Scans end at the listed blocks while the campaign was still active; no spoofed sale precedes the anchor on Ethereum since deployment or in the prior week on Base, Polygon and ApeChain.
